name: MANNI
description: Manni (meaning 'little man' or 'chap') is the national card game of Iceland, played with three players and a 48-card deck. The game features a unique 'Manni' - a spare hand of four cards dealt to the table that the declarer can use to improve their hand. With four different contracts (Grand, Spades, Other, and Nullo), players must play each contract once during the 12-deal game.

content.text: Manni (meaning 'little man' or 'chap') is the national card game of Iceland, played with three players and a 48-card deck. The game features a unique 'Manni' - a spare hand of four cards dealt to the table that the declarer can use to improve their hand. With four different contracts (Grand, Spades, Other, and Nullo), players must play each contract once during the 12-deal game.
Manni is the national card game of Iceland, with numerous local variations across the country. The name refers to the spare hand (Manni) that can be used to improve a player's hand.
3 players. Each plays individually in some contracts; in others, the declarer plays against the other two.
52 cards (Trjámann). Ranking: Ace (high), King, Queen, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (low). In Nullo contract Ace may be low in some variants.

items.text: Basic Manni: 48 cards (twos removed), 12 each, 12 to Manni. Trump rotates hearts, spades, diamonds, clubs. Player to dealer's left may exchange all 12 cards with Manni. Score: +1 per trick over 4; first to 10 points wins.

Trjámann: Full 52-card pack, 16 each, 4 to Manni. Declarer (left of dealer) chooses contract: Nullo, Grand, Spades, or Other. Declarer may discard up to 4 and draw from Manni. 12 deals; each player must play each contract once. Targets: 8/4/4 (Grand/Spades/Other) or 4/6/6 (Nullo).

Hornafjarðarmanni: 52 cards with twos. Deal: 4 to Manni, then 3 to each, repeated until Manni has 16 and each player 12. Cut card determines contract (ten+ no trump, 6-9 suit trump, 5 or lower nóló). Left of dealer may discard up to 7 and replace from Manni; right up to 5; dealer the rest. First to 10 positive points ends game; net score decides winner.

Laugavatnsmanni: Similar to Trjámann with six contracts (Nullo, Grand, Spades, Hearts, Clubs, Diamonds), 18 deals. Bidding: left of dealer chooses contract; others may take over with a 'great' contract (14 tricks for declarer, 1 each for opponents). Great contract outbid by denomination: Grand highest, then hearts, spades, diamonds, clubs.
